title: Ice at the boundary
prompt: An insulated cup holds 100 g of ice at 0 °C and 200 g of water at 30 °C. Use latent heat of fusion 334 J/g and liquid specific heat 4.18 J/(g K). Determine the final temperature and masses. Find the threshold initial water temperature required for the last ice to melt and use it to check the phase assumption.

answer:
Heat released by the 200 g of water cooling from \(30^\circ\text{C}\) to \(0^\circ\text{C}\):

\[
Q_{\text{cool}}=(200)(4.18)(30)=25080\ \text{J}
\]

Heat required to melt all 100 g of ice at \(0^\circ\text{C}\):

\[
Q_{\text{melt,all}}=(100)(334)=33400\ \text{J}
\]

Since \(25080 < 33400\), not all the ice melts. The final temperature is therefore

\[
\boxed{0^\circ\text{C}}
\]

Mass of ice melted:

\[
m_{\text{melted}}=\frac{25080}{334}\approx 75.09\ \text{g}
\]

Thus:

\[
m_{\text{ice,final}}=100-75.09\approx \boxed{24.91\ \text{g ice}}
\]

\[
m_{\text{water,final}}=200+75.09\approx \boxed{275.09\ \text{g water}}
\]

The threshold initial water temperature needed to just melt the last of the ice is found from

\[
m_w c \,(T_i-0)=m_{\text{ice}}L_f
\]

\[
T_i=\frac{(100)(334)}{(200)(4.18)}
=\frac{33400}{836}
\approx 39.95^\circ\text{C}
\]

So the threshold is

\[
\boxed{T_i \approx 39.95^\circ\text{C} \approx 40.0^\circ\text{C}}
\]

Since the actual initial water temperature is \(30^\circ\text{C}<39.95^\circ\text{C}\), there is not enough heat to melt all the ice. Therefore the phase assumption is consistent:

\[
\boxed{\text{Final state: }0^\circ\text{C},\quad 24.91\text{ g ice} + 275.09\text{ g liquid water.}}
\]

Equivalently, final mixture mass: \(\boxed{300.0\text{ g total}}\), with \(\boxed{275.09\text{ g liquid water}}\) and \(\boxed{24.91\text{ g ice}}\).
